title: Bonsai: patching the loaded model breaks on deleted elements and an empty output path
description:
Found in the user's Bonsai test of the recipe (endrawing-oy4), both in bim/module/patch/operator.py ExecuteIfcPatch.execute, and both affect any recipe run on the loaded model:

1. ifc_patch_output = props.ifc_patch_output or props.ifc_patch_input is '' when a model is loaded from memory and neither path is set, and ifcpatch.write(output, '') then raises 'failed to write to path: .', after the model has already been patched. Fix: skip the write when there is no output path, since the patched model is in memory and the user saves normally.

2. A recipe that deletes elements leaves Blender objects in IfcStore.id_map pointing at ids that no longer exist. The drawings list empties and saving fails in export_ifc.sync_object_placement with 'RuntimeError: Instance #29246 not found'. Fix: after patching the loaded model, drop IfcStore id_map/guid_map entries whose element is gone, remove those orphaned objects, and call bonsai.bim.handler.refresh_ui_data() so the lists rebuild.

Both fixes go on the same branch as separate commits, for the same pull request.
notes: Amended into commit dd405b468 on the local branch, three fixes in two files: (1) ExecuteIfcPatch writes only when an output path was given; (2) after patching the loaded model, purge_deleted_elements() drops IfcStore id_map/guid_map entries whose element is gone and removes the orphaned objects, then refresh_ui_data() and reload_drawing_lists() rebuild the drawing and sheet lists when open; (3) DocProperties.get_active_drawing() returns None for a removed drawing instead of raising, which was breaking every redraw of the drawings panel. The user confirmed (1) fixed; (2) and (3) await a re-test. ruff, black and py_compile clean, and all three verified loaded in Blender from the branch.

title: Cleanup deletes user-made sheets with Purpose 'General Arrangement'
description:
cleanup_existing_drawings() removes every IfcDocumentInformation whose Purpose is 'General Arrangement' and which it considers to have no drawings. Its has_drawings check looks for an IfcRelAssociatesDocument whose RelatingDocument is an IfcDocumentReference with ReferencedDocument == sheet. The DRAWING references that place drawings on a sheet are never associated to any object, so no sheet ever passes the check. Every sheet with that Purpose is deleted on every run, including sheets the user made themselves.

Verified: a user-created sheet (Identification GA-101, Purpose 'General Arrangement', Scope SHEET) with one of the user's own drawings on it was deleted on the first endrawing run.

This breaks the documented guarantee that only entities marked GeneratedBy = 'endrawing' are modified. Fix: identify generated sheets positively, for example by recording each generated sheet on its drawings (the drawings carry the GeneratedBy marker), or by only removing sheets whose DRAWING references all point at endrawing-generated drawings. Never infer ownership from Purpose alone. Add a regression test with a user sheet that has the same Purpose.
close_reason: Cleanup now traces everything it removes from GeneratedBy annotations: a sheet is removed only if it is a General Arrangement sheet whose DRAWING references all point at endrawing drawings. Also stops leaking drawing IfcDocumentInformation/references on every run, and no longer sweeps unrelated relationships or empty groups.

title: get_centroid() ignores project units and placement rotation
description:
Space labels are misplaced in any model that isn't in metres, and in any space whose placement is rotated.

get_centroid() calls ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape() with default settings. That returns vertices in local coordinates and SI metres. It then adds only the translation part of the space's ObjectPlacement, which is in project units, and ignores the placement's rotation.

Verified with a 4m x 2m x 3m space placed at (10, 20, 0) m, whose expected centroid is (2, 1, 1.5) m in local coordinates:
- metres, no rotation: expected (12, 21, 1.5), got (12, 21, 1.5)
- millimetres, no rotation: expected (12000, 21000, 1500), got (10002, 20001, 1.5)
- metres, rotated 90 deg about z: expected (9, 22, 1.5), got (12, 21, 1.5)

Fix: tessellate with use-world-coords and convert-back-units, so vertices are already world coordinates in project units, and drop the placement addition. It would also help to tessellate all spaces in one multithreaded ifcopenshell.geom.iterator pass, like get_element_bounds(), rather than calling create_shape() once per space. Note that the mean of the vertices isn't the true centroid: it's biased towards densely tessellated edges. Consider ifcopenshell.util.shape helpers or the bbox centre instead.
close_reason: get_centroid replaced by GeometryUtils.get_centroids: one iterator pass for all spaces in world coordinates and project units, volume centroid instead of vertex mean. Tests cover metres, millimetres, rotated placements and an L-shaped space.

title: get_bbox() x==0/y==0 skip is a fragile heuristic
description: endrawing.py:112-113 skips any element whose placement origin has x==0.0 or y==0.0. Intended to drop unplaced origin elements, but it silently discards legitimately placed elements landing on either world axis (e.g. building grid origin on x=0). Combined with the <2-element crash, over-filtering here can crash get_bbox. Use 'x==0 and y==0 and z==0' (only skip true origin) or detect identity/default placement.
close_reason: Fixed get_bbox origin skip and <2-element crash; added tests

title: get_bbox() crashes with fewer than 2 valid elements
description: In GeometryUtils.get_bbox (endrawing.py:94-138), bbox_min and bbox_max start as [] and fill lazily (bbox_min on the 1st valid element, bbox_max on the 2nd). If a location yields 0 or 1 qualifying element, bbox_max stays [] and the midpoint calc at line 132 (bbox_max[0]) throws IndexError. A building with a single placed element, or one where everything is filtered by the x==0/y==0 rule, hard-crashes. Needs a guard.
close_reason: Fixed get_bbox origin skip and <2-element crash; added tests

title: Recipe takes drawing paths from BBIM_Documentation
description: Read the IfcProject BBIM_Documentation pset (DrawingsDir, LayoutsDir, TitleblocksDir, StylesheetPath, MarkersPath, SymbolsPath, PatternsPath, ShadingStylesPath) as Bonsai's tool.Drawing get_default_*_path functions do. The pset is usually absent: Bonsai never writes it, it's a template the user adds by hand. So fall back per property, whenever the pset or that property is missing or empty, to Bonsai's shipped preference defaults (drawings/, layouts/, layouts/titleblocks/, drawings/assets/default.css, markers.svg, symbols.svg, patterns.svg, shading_styles.json), which are endrawing's current paths. Never read Blender preferences, so the output is the same standalone and in Bonsai. Sanitise SVG file names like Bonsai's sanitise_filename (alphanumerics and '._- ' only). Document in the Patcher docstring that the pset is how to customise paths. Tests: no pset, pset with only some properties, and a fully set pset.
close_reason: Commit c7f665c33 on the local IfcOpenShell branch (not pushed). DrawingGenerator.get_documentation_paths() reads the IfcProject BBIM_Documentation pset once, and each property falls back separately (missing or empty) to DOCUMENTATION_DEFAULTS, Bonsai's shipped defaults. Backslashes become /. get_path() joins a folder and a file name sanitised like Bonsai's sanitise_filename. Blender preferences are never read. Tests in src/ifcpatch/test/test_GenerateGeneralArrangementDrawings.py cover no pset, a partial pset with an empty value, a full pset with a Windows-style folder, and sanitising; the 78 endrawing tests still pass against the recipe through the shim.

title: Number drawings on a sheet from 1
description: Sheet DRAWING references get Identification '0', '1', ... because generate_drawings() starts drawing_id at 0. Industry convention, and Bonsai's AddDrawingToSheet (count of DRAWING/SCHEDULE/REFERENCE references + 1), number drawings on a sheet from 1. Start at 1 and add a test.
close_reason: generate_drawings() starts drawing_id at 1, so sheet DRAWING references are numbered 1..N like Bonsai's AddDrawingToSheet. Test added.

title: North arrow for plans of rotated buildings
description:
Since endrawing-991, plans of rotated buildings are square to the sheet (the user's decision, 2026-09-10), so north isn't up. Bonsai doesn't show the right north for them:
- Bonsai's A1/A2/A3 titleblocks have <g data-type="true-north"> and <g data-type="grid-north"> arrows, which sheeter.py build_titleblock rotates by -get_true_north() (and -get_grid_north()) for the whole project. Nothing accounts for a drawing's camera rotation, so on a rotated building's sheet the arrow is off by the building's rotation.
- bonsai/bim/data/assets/symbols.svg has no north arrow symbol (only tags, elevation/section arrows, setout/control/traverse points, spot-elevation), so endrawing can't just place a SYMBOL annotation (EPset_Annotation.Symbol) in each plan.

Options for the user to choose from:
1. Upstream Bonsai change: rotate the titleblock north arrows per sheet by the rotation of the plan drawings on it (endrawing sheets hold one building, so all its plans share one rotation), or support a per-drawing north.
2. Endrawing draws its own arrow in each rotated plan as annotation linework plus an 'N' text, placed in model coordinates so it points at true north.
3. Add a north-arrow symbol to Bonsai's symbols.svg (upstream) and have endrawing place a SYMBOL annotation.
Only rotated buildings are affected; unrotated plans are project-north-up as before, and the titleblock arrow is correct for them.
close_reason: Not for endrawing (user, 2026-09-11): placing a north arrow automatically is something users drawing by hand want too, so it belongs in lower-level tools (Bonsai/ifcopenshell), not in endrawing.

title: Generated drawing names can collide with other drawings' SVG paths
description: Drawing SVG paths are drawings/{annotation.Name}.svg, where plans are named after the storey (e.g. 'Ground Floor') and elevations '{building.Name} NORTH'. A user drawing with the same name, a drawing left over from an older endrawing version, or two buildings with the same storey names all map to the same SVG file, so generating one overwrites the other, and sheets referencing that Location show the wrong drawing. Cleanup also uses Location to decide which sheet references point at generated drawings. Bonsai avoids this with tool.Drawing.ensure_unique_drawing_name (bonsai/core/drawing.py add_drawing) and sanitises filenames with sanitise_filename. Fix: make generated drawing names unique across all IfcAnnotation drawings, e.g. prefix plans with the building name, and sanitise the path the way Bonsai does. Seen on courtyard/model.ifc, whose 80 pre-marker drawings share names with the ones endrawing now generates.
notes: Checked 2026-09-11. With uniquely named buildings, elevations ('{building} NORTH') and location plans ('{building} LOCATION') are already unique. Plans aren't: they're named after the storey alone, and every building normally has a 'Ground Floor', so two buildings share drawings/Ground Floor.svg (reproduced). Bonsai writes each drawing's SVG to its reference Location, so the last one generated overwrites the other and both sheets show it. Collisions with user-made drawings are unlikely, since Bonsai names plans '{STOREY} PLAN'. Likely fix: name plans '{building.Name} {storey.Name}', like the elevations. Waiting for the user's go-ahead because it renames drawings.
close_reason: Plans are named '{building.Name} {storey.Name}' (user's choice, 2026-09-11), like the elevations, so each building's 'Ground Floor' gets its own SVG path. Tested with two buildings that both have a 'Ground Floor'.

title: Align bboxes and cameras to building orientation; name elevations by nearest compass point
description:
Bounding boxes are aligned to the world axes, and the four elevation cameras always look along world +/-X and +/-Y. The elevations are named NORTH, SOUTH, EAST and WEST on the assumption that world +Y is north (FIXME at endrawing.py:932). For a building whose placement is rotated relative to the world axes:
- the bbox is oversized
- plan cameras are skewed relative to the building, so plans sit rotated on the sheet
- elevations see the facades obliquely instead of square on

The names also ignore true north. IFC world +Y is project north; true north is the Model context's TrueNorth, available from ifcopenshell.util.geolocation.get_true_north() (degrees, anticlockwise positive). There's also get_grid_north() if surveyor's grid north is wanted instead.

Scope: the building's orientation comes only from its placement, which is the correct way to model a rotated building in IFC (a local coordinate system for the building). Take the z rotation of the building's absolute placement (ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(building.ObjectPlacement), which includes any rotated site placement above it). If that rotation is zero, keep today's world-aligned behaviour. Don't try to infer orientation from geometry: if walls are rotated inside an unrotated building placement, the model is wrong, not endrawing.

Proposed approach:
1. Compute an oriented bbox in the building's frame by rotating vertices into that frame before taking min/max. get_element_bounds() returns world-aligned boxes per element, and rotating those afterwards inflates them. It needs to take each element's building rotation, which costs one numpy matmul per vertex buffer; elements normally belong to exactly one building.
2. Plans of rotated buildings are drawn square to the sheet (decided by the user, 2026-09-10): the plan camera's RefDirection is the building's x axis, so the building's own axes run parallel to the sheet edges. North is then no longer up, so the plan should show a north arrow for true north; check whether Bonsai already draws one or endrawing needs to add it. Place elevation cameras square on to each face of the oriented bbox. The site-wide location plan stays north-up.
3. Name each elevation by the compass bearing of its face's outward normal relative to true north, snapped to the nearest of eight compass points (45 degree sectors: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). Buildings within 22.5 degrees of orthogonal keep NORTH, SOUTH, EAST and WEST; buildings nearer 45 degrees get NORTH-EAST, SOUTH-EAST, SOUTH-WEST and NORTH-WEST. The four faces are 90 degrees apart, so round(bearing / 45) mod 8 moves in steps of 2 and the four names can never collide. Choose a deterministic tie-break at exactly 22.5 degrees, for example rounding towards the cardinal point. Naming by true north applies to unrotated buildings too.

Tests: building placements rotated 0, 30 and 45 degrees, a building rotated through its site's placement, a building with rotated walls but an unrotated placement (must stay world-aligned), and a model with a TrueNorth offset. Check the oriented bbox dimensions, camera directions (plan RefDirection = building x axis) and elevation names. When done, remove the FIXME and the Known Limitations entries in CLAUDE.md and README.md.
close_reason: Building orientation comes from the z rotation of its absolute placement (incl. site). Rotated buildings get oriented bboxes (vertices rotated into the building frame in the same tessellation pass), plans square to the building (RefDirection = building x), elevations square on to each face, and labels along the building x axis. Elevations are named by the bearing of the face normal from true north snapped to 8 compass points (ties go cardinal). Location plans stay north-up. No geometry inference. North arrow follow-up: endrawing-s5d.

title: Drawing documents and groups aren't nested under Bonsai's DRAWINGS parents
description:
Bonsai now organises drawings under shared parents (bonsai/core/drawing.py add_drawing; tool.Drawing.ensure_drawings_parent_document and ensure_drawings_parent_group):
- Each drawing's IfcDocumentInformation (Scope DRAWING) is created with api.document.add_information(parent=<DRAWINGS document>). That nests it, via IfcDocumentInformationRelationship, under an IfcDocumentInformation whose Identification, Name and Scope are all 'DRAWINGS'.
- Each drawing's IfcGroup (ObjectType DRAWING) is assigned to a parent IfcGroup whose Name and ObjectType are 'DRAWINGS'.

endrawing's attach_sheet() instead associates each drawing document directly with IfcProject through an IfcRelAssociatesDocument, and create_drawing_group() never assigns groups to the DRAWINGS group. So endrawing's drawings sit outside the structure Bonsai creates and expects. A minor difference: Bonsai sets the drawing document's Identification to 'X' and its Name to the drawing name, while endrawing uses the drawing name for both.

Already matching Bonsai: the sheet's DRAWING references (Location, Identification, Description 'DRAWING', ReferencedDocument = sheet) match AddDrawingToSheet, and the sheet document plus its LAYOUT and TITLEBLOCK references match add_sheet. These only need moving onto the API (endrawing-f7g).

Fix: create or reuse the DRAWINGS parent document and group the way Bonsai does, create drawing documents with add_information(parent=...), and assign drawing groups to the parent group. Cleanup must never remove the parents, since Bonsai-created drawings share them. It also needs checking that removing a generated drawing document cleans up its IfcDocumentInformationRelationship membership. Best done together with endrawing-f7g.
close_reason: Drawing documents are created with add_information(parent=DRAWINGS document) and drawing groups assigned to the DRAWINGS group, found or created as Bonsai does. Drawing documents use Identification X like Bonsai. Cleanup never removes the parents; removing a drawing document drops its IfcDocumentInformationRelationship membership (tested with a Bonsai drawing document under the same parent).

title: Use ifcopenshell.api instead of raw create* calls; IFC2X3 crashes
description:
Several places build IFC entities directly with positional attributes instead of going through ifcopenshell.api:
- ContextManager: createIfcGeometricRepresentationContext for the Plan context (use api.context.add_context)
- attach_sheet() and create_sheet_info(): createIfcDocumentInformation, createIfcDocumentReference (four calls), and IfcRelAssociatesDocument made with api.root.create_entity and then filled in by hand (use api.document.add_information, edit_information, add_reference, edit_reference and assign_document)
- cleanup_existing_drawings(): ifc_file.remove(rel) and hasattr(ReferencedDocument) checks

The positional calls assume IFC4 attribute layouts. Verified: on an IFC2X3 model, generate_drawings() fails with 'ValueError: entity instance of type IFC2X3.IfcDocumentReference has only 3 attributes but 5 attributes were provided'. The API handles the schema differences (DocumentId vs Identification, and ItemReference/Name vs Identification/Description; see Bonsai's tool.Drawing.generate_reference_attributes).

This overlaps with aligning the drawing/sheet structure with Bonsai (see the related issue), and would be simplest to do together. Add an IFC2X3 test.
close_reason: Contexts, sheets, drawing documents and references now go through ifcopenshell.api (context.add_context, document.add_information/edit_information/add_reference/edit_reference/assign_document), with IFC2X3 attribute names handled like Bonsai's generate_reference_attributes. IFC2X3 test added; cleanup has no raw remove calls left.

title: Storeys at identical elevation collide in storeys dict
description: endrawing.py:840-847 keys storeys[local_placement[2][3]] = ifc_storey by Z. Two storeys at the same elevation (mezzanines, split levels) silently overwrite, losing a drawing. Key by storey GlobalId and sort by elevation separately.
close_reason: Fixed: storeys now keyed in a list and sorted by elevation (no collision); get_centroid wrapped in try/except in create_space_labels to skip geometry-less spaces; building natsort key falls back to '' when Name is None. All covered by passing test suite (25 tests).

title: get_centroid() has no failure handling for geometry-less spaces
description: ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape() (endrawing.py:150-151) raises if a space has no geometry representation. create_space_labels calls get_centroid for every space without try/except, so one geometry-less space aborts the whole run. Wrap and skip on failure.
close_reason: Fixed: storeys now keyed in a list and sorted by elevation (no collision); get_centroid wrapped in try/except in create_space_labels to skip geometry-less spaces; building natsort key falls back to '' when Name is None. All covered by passing test suite (25 tests).

title: get_bbox() measures placement origins, not geometry extents
description: endrawing.py:103-110 computes the bbox from each element's local-placement translation only. True footprint extends beyond outermost insertion point by wall length/thickness, so bbox is undersized and cameras can clip building edges. Related to but distinct from the rotation FIXME at line 834. Use ifcopenshell.geom bounds or actual shape vertices.
notes: Investigated the suggested fix (ifcopenshell.geom shape vertices / iterator bounds). Benchmarked: full tessellation costs ~0.05-0.10s per element even multithreaded with disable-opening-subtractions and coarse deflection. get_bbox runs once over all buildings plus once per building, so a real model (e.g. tamar, 4236 elements) would spend several minutes just computing the bbox before any drawing is generated. courtyard.ifc (2389 elems) took 356s for a single all-buildings pass. The original placement-origin approach is a DELIBERATE performance choice for an interactive save-time tool. Geometry-accurate bbox via tessellation is not viable here. Leaving open: a cheaper fix would be heuristic padding of the placement bbox (the site bbox already pads 2m), or reading cheap representation bounds where available, rather than meshing every element.
close_reason: Abandoned: iterating all geometry vertices via ifcopenshell is too slow to be practical

title: Archive the endrawing repo with a pointer to the ifcpatch recipe
description: Once the recipe is in v0.9.0 and checked in Bonsai: rewrite README.md to point at GenerateGeneralArrangementDrawings and show the ifcpatch CLI and Bonsai Patch panel usage, keep the history, and archive the GitHub repo.

title: Drawings from pre-GeneratedBy endrawing versions are duplicated on re-run
description: Models processed by endrawing before the GeneratedBy marker existed (e.g. homemaker-data courtyard/model.ifc: 80 DRAWING and 168 TEXT annotations, 80 DRAWING documents and 11 SHEET documents with no Purpose) keep their old drawings forever: they carry no marker, so cleanup rightly leaves them, and each run adds a full new set next to them. Needs a decision from the user: leave as is (users delete the old set by hand in Bonsai), or add an explicit opt-in (e.g. --adopt-legacy) that marks drawings matching endrawing's old naming and structure. Must not become an automatic heuristic, since it would risk deleting user drawings.
close_reason: Won't fix (user, 2026-09-11): endrawing hasn't had extensive use, so drawings from pre-GeneratedBy versions don't need handling.

title: Default drawing scale ignores imperial unit systems
description:
The default scale is always 1:100 (Scale '1/100', HumanScale '1:100'), even for imperial projects. Bonsai's own add_drawing defaults imperial projects to Scale '1/96' with HumanScale 1/8"=1'-0" (bonsai/core/drawing.py add_drawing, via tool.Drawing.get_unit_system()). The --scale option also always writes HumanScale as '1:N', which reads oddly for imperial scales.

Fix: when --scale isn't given, choose the default from the project's length unit (imperial -> 96), and format HumanScale in architectural notation for imperial projects, matching Bonsai. The location plan's 10x multiplier may need a sensible imperial equivalent too.
close_reason: Default scale follows the project length unit like Bonsai: 1/100 metric, 1/96 (1/8"=1'-0") imperial (any non-SI length unit). Imperial HumanScale uses Bonsai's architectural/engineering notation table, falling back to 1:N; the 10x location plan gives 1/960 = 1"=80'. --scale defaults to None.

title: Storeys and Include filters select buildings by Name, merging duplicate names
description:
generate_drawings() finds a building's storeys with selector 'IfcBuildingStorey, location="{building.Name}"', and the elevation and location-plan Include filters in EPset_Drawing use location="{building.Name}". So two buildings sharing a Name (common in merged or generated models, such as repeated plot names) would each get the other's storeys on their sheet, and their elevations would include both buildings. This is from reading the code; I haven't tested it with a model.

Bounding boxes no longer have this problem: they use get_decomposition() since d3250c5. Fix storeys the same way, by walking the building's decomposition. For the Include filters, which Bonsai evaluates as selector strings, check whether the selector can match a location by GlobalId instead of Name.
close_reason: Storeys are found by walking the building's decomposition, and elevation and location plan Include filters use location="{GlobalId}", which the selector matches as well as Name. Tested with two buildings named Plot.

title: natsorted building sort assumes Name is set
description: endrawing.py:276-278 sorts buildings with key=lambda x: x.Name. A building with Name==None breaks natsort comparison. Use 'x.Name or empty-string' fallback.
close_reason: Fixed: storeys now keyed in a list and sorted by elevation (no collision); get_centroid wrapped in try/except in create_space_labels to skip geometry-less spaces; building natsort key falls back to '' when Name is None. All covered by passing test suite (25 tests).
